_readme: turn-budgets.json — how many turns a build run gets (DRE-3097).
THE INCIDENT. agent-task.yml carried `--max-turns 150` as a literal.
DRE-3088 died at it three times in a row on 2026-09-04 ($19.12, $19.12,
$17.53); every one of those runs reached `⏳ 3/5 implementation green` and
died in the two steps after it, and the third death came AFTER the card had
been split to XS. Splitting did not help because the cost was never the size
of the change — it was the size of the file the agent has to read and re-read
(plan.yml is ~1,850 lines). The park receipt already named the other remedy,
'or raises the turn budget', and there was no handle on it.
THE DEFAULT IS 400, FOR EVERY RUN (DRE-4361, 2026-09-23, on the CEO's
instruction). The evidence: in 22 days no run died at 400 (26 runs), and
every one of the 110 turn-cap deaths was at 150. There is no footprint rung
to choose any more — one ceiling, everything gets it, and the 120-minute job
wall clock is unchanged and remains the real ceiling. `allowed` keeps all
three rungs because a card may still ask DOWNWARDS with a `turns:` label
(the epic's PROOF card plants its deaths with turns:150).
THE RULE: THE SET IS THE GUARD. The turn count is a KNOB and the run's own
cap is the GUARD — a card picks a rung, it does not name a number. `allowed`
is a closed, ordered set of reviewed rungs, exactly the way membership of a
model ladder in models.yaml is a reviewed spend decision. A `turns:` label
carrying anything else is refused, out loud, and the card falls back to what
it would otherwise have got. Raising the ceiling changes the bill only for
the runs that today produce nothing at all: --max-turns is a ceiling, not a
target, and a card that finishes in 90 turns costs 90 turns' worth whatever
the ceiling says.
DECIDE-BY. `decide_by_fraction` x the ceiling, rounded down, never below 10,
is the turn by which the build agent must have decided to continue or hand
back: 400 → 80, 250 → 50, 150 → 30. At 400 the ceiling is no longer the
thing that catches a lost agent, so the checkpoint is named instead.
WHY A FILE, not a lookup: the same constraint models.yaml and repo-map.json
are documented under in config/README.md — the workflows that read this run
in a product repo's Actions with no AWS credentials and no token for a
private repo, so selection must resolve out of the public .bureau-pipeline
checkout the workflow already does.
Read through scripts/turn_budget.py, never parsed inline. An unreadable file
degrades to the default map in that module rather than failing a build.

rungs.150: what every card ran on before DRE-4361, and no longer the default. Reachable only by a card that asks for it with a turns:150 label — the epic's PROOF card does exactly that to plant a turn-cap death.
rungs.250: the middle rung, likewise reachable only by an explicit turns:250 label. It was the first raise DRE-3097 offered, and no card is put on it automatically any more.
rungs.400: the default for every run (DRE-4361). Nothing above it: past here the answer is a smaller card, and the job's 120-minute wall clock is the real ceiling anyway.

size_note: size:XS…size:XL mean EFFORT (config/planning-shapes.json) and already sit on the board. They all map onto 400 now: with one ceiling for everything there is no rung for a size to choose, and a card carrying a size must never be budgeted BELOW a card carrying none. The key stays so a card's size can never be read as a request for less.
